Finding things out

What did the measurement miss?

Two different things can look the same through one kind of measurement.

A closer lookOpen the shared interactive reader ↗

The interactive example has its own motion control. Scroll inside it if you need more room.

An overview of the current research

Imagine two repeating signals that reach the same height. A measuring tool that keeps only their heights may report the same result, even if the signals rise and fall at different times.

Try the two views beside this story. The extra timing reference reveals a difference the first view left out. The drawing explains an idea; it is not a recording from an experiment.

Switch between the views. Look for a difference the first view misses.

Words used here
phase
Where a repeating signal is in its cycle: for example, whether it is rising or falling at a given moment.
detector
A tool or method that turns something happening into a record we can inspect.
Read the fuller explanation

Sometimes the next discovery begins by preserving a distinction the instrument discarded. More data from the same narrow view may never reveal it.

Choose a different way of looking. What becomes visible?

Where this comes from: What measurements miss

Current research synthesis

An overview of the current research

Asks which differences our measurements leave out and how another measurement might reveal them. It does not identify a new physical theory as true.

Read the full source note

The admissibility frontier

Experiments can erase phase, delay, boundary order, orientation and correlations. The programme asks which distinguishing records an apparatus could preserve. The physical identification of the proposed structures remains open.
